For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the vegetable Oils came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as vegetable Oils

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers vegetable Oils in 2 forms kept separate in every comparison: vegetable Oils, oil (761 results) and vegetable Oils, as sold (116 results).<sup <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-vegetable-oils" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-vegetable-oils-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of vegetable oils, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach vegetable Oils

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach vegetable Oils comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Vegetable Oils, oil from industrial had Fe higher at 23,700 µg/kg, against 11,300 µg/kg for industrial in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mehri F, Heshmati A, Talebi Ghane E, Khazaei M, Mahmudiono T, Fakhri Y · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">A probabilistic health risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in edible vegetable oils consumed in Hamadan, Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for vegetable Oils

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>

<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mehri F, Heshmati A, Talebi Ghane E, Khazaei M, Mahmudiono T, Fakhri Y · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">A probabilistic health risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in edible vegetable oils consumed in Hamadan, Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing vegetable Oils for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>
<a id="which-methods-species-measurements-validation-evidence-and-reporting-limits-are-needed"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-027"></a>
<a id="what-can-a-certificate-of-analysis-or-non-detect-establish-and-what-remains-untested"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 2 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 4,000 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Reporting limits for cadmium ranged from 0.1 µg/kg (Alrajhi et al. 2020) to 1,200 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/alrajhi2020-riyadh-edible-oils-trace-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ibrahim Mohammed Alrajhi, Hajo Idriss · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/alrajhi2020-riyadh-edible-oils-trace-metals">Concentration of Trace Metals in Some Major Edible Oils of so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span A useful lot result names the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below the limit that applies.



<a id="procurement-and-process-control"></a>
## Buying and verifying vegetable Oils

<a id="hmi-ing-028"></a>
<a id="what-origin-traceability-processing-and-analytical-information-should-a-buyer-request"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-029"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-030"></a>
<a id="what-supplier-process-or-test-result-changes-should-trigger-investigation-or-requalification"></a>

No maximum level for metals in vegetable Oils was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from vegetable Oils

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>
<a id="how-do-inclusion-rate-processing-yield-preparation-and-other-ingredients-affect-a-finished-product-estimate"></a>

<a id="what-conclusions-require-finished-product-measurements-or-a-separate-exposure-assessment"></a>

No source in the library converted vegetable Oils concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

Every source record that names vegetable Oils was decided on its content: 23 occurrence extracted, 23 records in all. The occurrence table renders every extracted result; held values remain visible with their reason.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.


<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Vegetable Oils FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-vegetable-oils" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-vegetable-oils" data-question="What heavy metals are found in vegetable Oils?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in vegetable Oils?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, Ba, K, Na and Tl in vegetable Oils, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal Heshmati A, Talebi Ghane E, Khazaei M, Mahmudiono T, Fakhri Y · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">A probabilistic health risk <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-vegetable-oils" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-vegetable-oils" data-question="How do heavy metals get into vegetable Oils?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into vegetable Oils?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, vegetable Oils from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than vegetable Oils from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mehri F, Heshmati A, Talebi Ghane E, Khazaei M, Mahmudiono T, Fakhri Y · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">A probabilistic health risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in edible vegetable oils consumed in Hamadan, Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Vegetable Oils, oil from industrial had lead higher at 27 µg/kg, against 13 µg/kg for industrial in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mehri F, Heshmati A, Talebi Ghane E, Khazaei M, Mahmudiono T, Fakhri Y · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">A probabilistic health risk assessment of potentially toxic elements in edible vegetable oils consumed in Hamadan, Iran</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">BMC Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mehri2024-vegetable-oils-iran-hamadan-ptes">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-vegetable-oils" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-vegetable-oils" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in vegetable Oils?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in vegetable Oils?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, vegetable Oils, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in SEARO (30 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (40 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-vegetable-oils" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-vegetable-oils" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in vegetable Oils?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in vegetable Oils?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same vegetable Oils.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Vegetable Oils, oil (GEMS/Food contaminants database) had cadmium lower at 2.5 µg/kg, against 4.4 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (vegetable oils, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-vegetable-oils-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-vegetable-oils-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in vegetable Oils is inorganic?">

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 8 results from 5 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span
